## Profile

Associate Professor, Department of Law, Faculty of Law, Seikei University. I specialize in economic law (antimonopoly and competition law). I received my LL.B. from Aoyama Gakuin University, my LL.M. from the Graduate School of Law at Aoyama Gakuin University (Private Law), and completed the doctoral program at the Graduate School of Law, Kyoto University (Legal and Political Theory). Ph.D. in Law.

My research focuses on digital market regulation, in particular self-preferencing by platforms, adtech, and the regulation of competitive conduct mediated by algorithms, which I examine comparatively across Japan, the United States, and the EU. I also work on the goals and interpretation of competition law (formalism and competition law, neo-Brandeisianism).

## Research interests

Antimonopoly law, U.S. antitrust law and EU competition law; digital platforms; self-preferencing; the goals of competition law (formalism, neo-Brandeisianism); private monopolization; unfair trade practices; blockchain and antimonopoly law; the intersection of labor markets and antimonopoly law; refusal to deal; predatory pricing
